findings.text: Three of the four done-when cases -- the JSON-list gate derivation, the manifest that appears a few seconds late, and the manifest that never appears -- are asserted only by tests/gate_review_promotion_test.py, which is not tracked at the reviewed head (git ls-tree 7e7251cb6a returns nothing for it) and lives only under /tmp scratch; deleting _await_review_manifest at promotion_checks.py:481, or reverting the unconditional resolved_gate.update at promotion_records.py:379, reddens no test in the repository, so the node's two largest behaviours have no regression guard once the scratch tree is gone.

The fragment states the gate arm runs '4 passed' at head against '2 failed, 2 passed' at base, and the manifest's artifacts and landing lines repeat that figure, but logs/gate-base.log -- the log the manifest cites -- records '3 failed, 1 passed in 8.93s'; the number is understated by one, so a coordinator landing this record on the plan lands a figure its own evidence contradicts.

The fragment says the negative control 'removes the gate derivation and case 1 is refused again ... 2 failed, 2 passed', but logs/negative-control.log records a different mutation ('_with_derived_total reduced to return body') and a different result ('2 failed, 16 passed'), and in it test_case1_no_gate_flags_with_a_json_list_tests_field passes -- so the clause the done_when names, that the first case is refused again under the control, is not shown by the control that was actually recorded.

_with_derived_total duplicates reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:2867 _with_a_derived_total: both are the same 'return the record unchanged when it carries an integer total, else review_module._derive_landed_total(body)' guard under two names in two modules, with two near-identical docstrings; the owner is reckon/crew/review.py:965 _derive_landed_total and one shared helper beside it would keep the two copies from diverging.

The comment introducing REVIEW_MANIFEST_WAIT_SECONDS names a specific review run id and a 'measured across nine reviews in one night' incident in a different file's comment, which is changelog prose in source: once the run directory is cleaned the reference resolves to nothing, and the sentence that actually justifies twenty seconds -- that a review is promoted the moment its record parses while the worker writes its manifest a few seconds later -- carries the reason without it.

_default_gate_evidence_from_manifest now applies _review_record_check unconditionally, so a review run promoted with an explicit --gate-command and --gate-log-path has both replaced by 'test -s <record>' and the record path; the done_when covers only the no-gate-flags case and no test exercises the explicit-flag case, so an operator who hands a review promotion its own check silently loses it.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 2266993b74; 8da2d7f8ff, 9c7ab88a12, b13dfd993c, b1ff2a15a2, e02ad76d12 and 9d9e1bf889 change the three modules and the refusal case, 7e7251cb6a changes only the 8-line evidence fragment, for 225 insertions and 18 deletions across five files.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names four cases, both arms as git checkouts under the run's scratch, EXIT= on every log and zero added failures; the recorded gate logs show 4 passed at head and 3 failed/1 passed at base, the suite pair is 438 passed base against 439 passed head, and the negative control records 2 failed/16 passed, though the control exercises the total derivation rather than the case 1 refusal the done_when names.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that a review run's promotion derives its own gate and total; reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:361-380 now takes the gate from the stored record for every review-role run, and reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:432 plus reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:2882 derive the total at each copy a promotion reads.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it states status complete, names five changed paths and seven commits, records both arm logs and ends them in EXIT=, and its artifacts and landing lines report the base gate arm as '2 failed/2 passed' where logs/gate-base.log records '3 failed, 1 passed'.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the dispatch fence named four paths; the live pointer's node.write_paths now names six, adding reckon/crew/promotion_records.py and tests/test_a_review_refusal_names_its_failed_condition.py, and every path in the diffstat is inside that widened grant.
